chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Abdullah ibn Abu Ya'foor, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah

A man who believes in your guardianship, exempts himself from your enemy, permits what you have permitted, prohibits what you have prohibited, and claims that the authority is still with you and has not passed to others, except that he says: They have disagreed among themselves while they are the leading Imams. If they agree upon a man and say 'This is he,' we say 'This is he.' He said: If he dies upon this opinion, he has died a death of ignorance (jahiliyyah).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who believes in the Imams but doubts their specific identity through consensus?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the critical issue of *al-Ghaybah al-Kubra* (the Major Occultation), where the certainty of the Imam's identity was replaced by scholarly consensus (*ijma'*). Imam al-Sadiq (as) warns that while holding core beliefs is essential, introducing doubt about the Imam's lineage or authority by claiming they disagreed on succession constitutes a major deviation, equating it to the pre-Islamic state of *Jahiliyyah*. This establishes the theological boundary between acceptable interpretive variance and fundamental disbelief regarding the continuity of divine guidance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (16) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Rabah from Ahmad bin Ali al-Himyari from al-Hasan bin Ayyoob from Abdul Kareem bin Amr al-Khath’ami that Abdullah bin Abu Ya’foor had said: I said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as):

“Someone believes in your guardianship, exempts himself from your enemy, permits what you have permitted, refrains from what you have prohibited and thinks that the imamate is still among you and will never go to other than you but he says: They (the infallible imams) have disagreed among themselves while they are the leading imams. If they agree upon a man and say that it is he (the imam), we will say that it is he.” Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) said: If this someone remains with this opinion, he will die as an unbeliever.
